raw_response:
I have been farming these 14 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I never went to school, but I know my land better than any book. I am 59 now and I work this farm alone, so I cannot chase every new idea — I stick to what my hands and my neighbors have proven.

My wheat is already in the ground from last autumn — 3 mu of an improved variety that my neighbor Lao Wang recommended years ago. It has never let me down. I will irrigate it three times from the well this spring: once when it greens up, once at jointing, and once when the heads fill. I spread about one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu at the start, and half a bag of urea at topdressing. I spray twice for insects and weeds. I expect about 950 jin per mu, same as last year.

Garlic takes 2 mu. I save my own cloves every year — why buy seed when your own bulbs are good? It needs water four times, especially in April when the bulbs are swelling. I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. I spray three times to keep the leaf rot away. If the frost does not hit hard, I should get 3,000 jin per mu.

Chili is my main crop and my biggest worry — 4 mu. I buy hybrid seedlings from the market in late April because they are stronger against disease. Chili drinks a lot of water, so I irrigate six times through the summer. I learned ten years ago that you cannot skip spraying — the aphids will ruin everything — so I spray about ten times. I put more fertilizer on chili than anything else, especially potash for the fruit. I hope for 4,000 jin per mu.

Cotton is on 2 mu. I plant hybrid seeds in late April. It does not need as much water as chili — three irrigations is enough. But the bollworms never sleep, so I spray eight times. One bag of compound fertilizer per mu is what I always use. I expect around 500 jin of seed cotton per mu.

Watermelon fills the last 3 mu. I buy hybrid seeds and plant them in early May. Watermelon is tricky with water — too much and the fruit splits, too little and they stay small. I irrigate four times, carefully. I spray five times for insects and mildew. I expect about 4,500 jin per mu.

I rotary-till everything now. I do not have draft animals anymore, and rotary is faster. I am just one person, so I hire a few days of help at harvest time, but otherwise I do it all myself. This plan is tight, but it is what I know, and it keeps me fed and with some cash in my pocket.
